issues.problem: When the agencies disagree, the fire card's official record section gives CAL FIRE a status that is not CAL FIRE's. Example: the Timber Fire, active in NIFC but not in CAL FIRE. The section headed 'CAL FIRE incident record' says 'Status Active' and 'Updated by CAL FIRE …'. Two lines lower, the disagreement block says 'Not listed as active (CAL FIRE, …)'. OfficialRecord takes the status from fireStatus(fire) / isActiveFire(fire) on the merged row (mode 'live', is_active true because NIFC lists it). It does not use the record's own status (ownRecordActive / recordBlocks()[0].is_active). This breaks the official-information rule (each statement keeps its issuer) and the user's decision 2 in round 3 ('each agency's record with its own issuer, status and time'; the brief names the Timber Fire as its example). The map hover in web/src/map/mapController.ts:1443 has the same fault: 'CAL FIRE (official): … · 97 % contained · Active'.
issues.evidence: Live list on API 8712 (FIRE3D_LIVE=0): 2026-timber-fire-b7e4a3 has record_source 'calfire', active_sources ['wfigs'], mode 'live', is_active true. 2026-rocky-fire-f65c7d is the same. Fire card text in Chrome: '.fc-official' = 'CAL FIRE incident record | 25,352 ac | 97% | Status Active | Updated by CAL FIRE Oct 20, 8:41 PM PDT (2 d ago) | The agencies' records differ … | Not listed as active (CAL FIRE, updated Oct 20, 8:41 PM PDT) | Timber: Active (USFS (USDA Forest Service) via NIFC WFIGS, …)'. Rocky reads 'CAL FIRE incident record | 1.0 ac | 100% | Status Active | Updated by CAL FIRE Sep 14, 6:22 AM PDT (39 d ago) | … Not listed as active (CAL FIRE, …)'. Screenshot: docs/screenshots/review3-us-web-firecard-timber-desktop.png. The Timber case in FireCard.test.ts asserts only the block lines, so it passes.
issues.fix: In OfficialRecord, take the record's own status from ownRecordActive(fire) (exported by web/src/api/records.ts) or blocks[0].is_active, never from the merged row. When the record is not active: the status reads 'Contained' at 100 % or with contained_ms, else 'Not listed as active', and the time line uses the '<issuer> record last edited …' wording. The ACTIVE chip in the title is outside .fc-official and may stay, because Fire-3d lists the fire as active when either agency says so. In the mapController hover, use the record's own status after recordIssuerLabel(s), and add e.g. 'active per NIFC WFIGS' when the listing status differs. Extend the Timber test in FireCard.test.ts: .fc-official contains neither 'Status Active' nor 'Updated by CAL FIRE', and it contains 'Not listed as active'.

issues.problem: The hover on an evacuation zone always says 'Official status from local officials via Cal OES.' (line 1463). us-official's brief-3 work adds Oregon OEM zones (source_id 'or_oem_evacuations', aggregator 'Oregon OEM') to the same map layer. A hover on an Oregon zone would therefore name the wrong aggregator. §14.8.5 requires issuer and aggregator to come from sources[]. us-web edited this hover block in brief 3 (it passed tf to zoneDetail), but the Cal OES sentence is unchanged from brief 2. The bug is latent today: the live Oregon layer is empty off-season (us-official known issue), so only fire-season zones would show it.
issues.evidence: mapController.ts:1456-1464: line('Official status from local officials via Cal OES. Fire-3d forecasts are not evacuation instructions.'). extras/evacuation.ts exports zoneSourceId(p) and aggregatorOf(data, sourceId) ('Cal OES' / 'Oregon OEM').
issues.fix: Use `const agg = aggregatorOf(useExtrasRuntime.getState().evac.data ?? null, zoneSourceId(zone.properties))` and write 'Official status from local officials via ${agg}. …'. Move the hover text into a small pure helper with a unit test for one California zone and one Oregon zone.

issues.problem: Per-run skill table (V-R13): when the run has growth values (validation will write growth_sorensen), the total column's header is only 'Total-area overlap'. The words '(includes the area already burned at the start)' that §14.4 asks for appear only in a hover tooltip on 'Sørensen'. The full header shows only when there are no growth values, which is today's case. No unit test covers SkillTable (growth first, the header, the neutral bars).
issues.evidence: AnalysisTab.tsx:311: <th>{growth ? 'Total-area overlap' : 'Total-area overlap (includes the area already burned at the start)'}</th>. grep finds no test file that renders SkillTable or 'Total-area'.
issues.fix: Keep the §14.4 wording visible in both cases, for example as a short footnote under the table when the header is shortened. Add an SSR test: a manifest with growth_sorensen shows the Growth column first, the total label and the tone-neutral bars; one without it shows 'The growth score (new spread only) is not stored for this run.'

issues.problem: The screen does not credit the new national sources whose data it shows. The fire card shows NWCG agency names ('C&L (County and Local)'). The location card shows the county and state from Census TIGERweb ('Place: Fulton County, GA') and the time zone line from USDOT BTS NTAD. No UI line credits 'Agency names: NWCG unit identifiers', 'Boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau TIGERweb' or 'Time zones: USDOT BTS NTAD' (§14.13). §14.13 assigns only SPEC and README, so the UI placement is unassigned.
issues.evidence: grep -rn 'NTAD|TIGERweb|NWCG' web/src (non-test) finds no user-facing credit. The Gazetteer credit is present ('Towns and ZIP areas: U.S. Census Bureau Gazetteer Files.').
issues.fix: Add a credit line under 'Updated and reliability' in the overview location card ('Place and time zone: U.S. Census Bureau TIGERweb; USDOT BTS NTAD'). Add one under the fire card's record when an agency name is shown ('Agency names: NWCG unit identifiers'). Alternatively, the integration or final verification adds them to the app credits.
